recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Follow-up is only needed in the Extension Pack if the deprecated legacy minValueSet/maxValueSet extension definitions themselves need maintenance; no core FHIR source fix is indicated for FHIR-6087.
issue_request: FHIR-6087 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for a way to specify multiple ElementDefinition bindings with different strengths; the accepted resolution was to define a minimum binding as well as the existing maximum binding extension.
initial_application: Git f092fc9e6abb30821694905a88b5b94322440710, matching the Jira svn revision 6376 comment, added the #6087 minValueSet extension. The companion maxValueSet extension already existed from git 4c67059737b5717deeb45b22208117dde839a652.
additional_context: Later same-artifact decisions, especially FHIR-8723 and FHIR-9195, led to a broader additional-binding model. Current core source lists ElementDefinition as an active type; ElementDefinition.binding.additional is 0..*; terminology prose documents additional bindings, maximum/minimum purposes, and multiple applicable bindings where meaningful. The old minValueSet and maxValueSet extension definitions now live in the Extension Pack as retired/deprecated definitions that point users to additionalBinding.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current R5+ ElementDefinition.binding.additional model is the correct current representation of the seed's min/max binding need and broader multiple-binding use cases; reintroducing or duplicating legacy extension text in core would be misleading.
